title: Kelly Oubre Jr. to sign 2-year contract with Pacers: How he helps Indiana
author: David Aldridge
content:
The Indiana Pacers and wing Kelly Oubre Jr. have agreed on a two-year, $16.5 million contract, according to team sources who spoke on condition of anonymity because the deal has not been completed. The deal will be fully guaranteed, per league sources.

The potential for significant minutes at small forward factored into Oubre’s decision, the sources said.

Pacers general manager Chad Buchanan said last week that wing was one of two positions, along with center, that his team needed to prioritize this offseason.

“If you look at our bench right now, I think you kind of see where we have proven veteran players at,” Buchanan said in his post-draft news conference last week. “The wing position would probably be one (to evaluate). If we can add some wing depth that would help.”

Oubre brings legitimate size on the wing, which should improve Indiana’s perimeter defense. Oubre, who averaged 14.1 points in 50 regular-season games with the Philadelphia 76ers last season, also adds a scoring punch off the bench. He excels as a cutter, which should pair well with star point guard Tyrese Haliburton, who missed the entire 2025-26 season due to a torn right Achilles he suffered in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals. Haliburton also came down with shingles in February and was managing that amid his Achilles rehab.

“I look back at videos of me, and I can see how swollen my face is (from the medicine),” Haliburton recently told reporters at his annual youth camp. “I’m glad that, that’s beyond me (and) past me now. I feel great. Body feels great. I’m able to do everything. I feel like I’m operating like I’m a healthy NBA player for the first time in a long time.”

The Pacers are confident that with a healthy Haliburton rejoining their established core, they can get back into title contention. But Oubre’s deal puts the franchise in rare financial territory. Indiana will use a chunk of its non-taxpayer midlevel exception to sign him. The agreement puts the team $6.5 million above the luxury-tax line and a mere $1 million below the first apron with 14 roster spots filled. Historically, the Pacers have never paid the tax — it was a key reason the franchise did not re-sign Myles Turner last summer.

Oubre’s presence will also raise questions about the roles of 2023 first-round draft picks Jarace Walker and Ben Sheppard, who were selected eighth and 26th, respectively. Both wings have had up-and-down careers in Indiana, and they’ve yet to solidify themselves as surefire pieces of the future. Both are set to become restricted free agents next year.

If Indiana can offload Walker’s salary via a trade this offseason, it would give the Pacers exactly enough room to get below the tax line.

“We’re also working under a new financial system, so there’s some limitations there with the apron and everything like that,” Buchanan said last week of the Pacers’ free-agency decisions. “So, if it’s the right player and it’s the right move for the team, we’re gonna do it. But we’re not gonna try to disrupt this group.”
